tips.comment: Schmilsson won on his first attempt over fences here despite not jumping well. Held up at the back nor at the last fence after taking the lead. Up seven pounds in the weights with Sean Bowen riding again. He should win again, hopefully with a better jumping performance.
Won a decent little race last time and goes up 3lb for a 3l win. That was a truly run race with rivals running to their marks, so should have a chance of following up here

The model I run suggests Salamanca Bay can win this one. Salamanca Bay lines up with a comparably high RPR in what looks like a relatively open 6-horse race. Salamanca Bay looks well treated off this mark with an official rating, leaving it carrying 9 lbs less than the current market leader and 1 stone 5 lbs less than the top weight around this 2m trip. Has got some form to show with recent figures of 73-2, and with that 2nd place coming 26 days ago, Bryan Hughes looks to steer Salamanca Bay over the line in first this time. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, largely driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Emily Love easily lost her maiden tag at Limerick last time in a 15 horse maiden and she should get her second win here at Perth with Sean Bowen booked to ride.

Wrecking Ballbilly comes from a yard that pulled off a big gamble in a race in England yesterday, and the horses are running well. The selection is probably fighting for each-way money here, but the jockey booking is eye-catching.
Won at 50-1 last time out by some clear 6 lengths (2m4f good ground. Same here today). If she can back that form up, she is one of the main players in this field.

Emily Love might take some beating, but Moonbow, owned by J Fyffe and Mrs W Duffus, could be at Perth today to see their gelding running a big race. Brian Hughes is on top of his game once more. He might not have gone off, but he is a good judge of pace, which can see him pushing the gelding into the lead and possibly making all. Perth can be suited to front runners with slight bends in the course, making the course feel easier. He won at Catterick and can do the same tactics here, with trainer Patrick Neville winning with his first of two horses at Perth today.

BLAZING COURT (20/1) was doing well chasing last year but reverted back to hurdles in November. He's a consistent sort who often makes the frame in both codes. It's evident that he needs a run after a break to fire on all cylinders. He's had two respectable runs last month, so I expect he'll improve again today under claimer John Dixon (7lb allowance), who knows how to handle him.

Very nicely bred horse who made a winning debut on the flat for D. Mensuisier, but lost their way afterwards. Did not win in this sphere for previous trainer A. Dunn, but did run some good races in defeat @ this level. Making stable today off dropping mark of 92, good conditional up claiming 3lb and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 40/1 worth Ew consideration here against hot favourite.

Hood on for the first time and a chance taken that it might make a significant difference. Jockey is on a good run with three winners in the last two weeks from only fifteen rides. Hasn't been able to put a run of races together for a while, and this is now the third run back after the latest break, so should be the fittest in a while. The fourth at Kelso last time was the best run so far.

The Flying Poet was a decent second last time out after a break, with the winner going on to win again in C4 since. My pick goes again off the same mark today, with more expected now second up and Sean Bowen back in the saddle .

Was well beaten on his first two starts for this yard and finished just outside the places on his next two but improved to win over today's trip at Hexham eighteen days ago. Dylan Johnston's 3lb claim should help. Should be involved at the finish.

EVIES COURT runs for a yard who landed a huge gamble yesterday and in general trainer Noel Kelly does well with what he sends across from Ireland. This young mare may have improved significantly during her time spent on the sidelines through the winter and second-up for this campaign today she could show more.

The model I run suggests Burgundy Man can cause an upset here. Burgundy Man has a very high price here at 34s, so clearly isn't fancied by the early market. This model result has been driven by Burgundy Man having the joint highest RPR for this 11-runner race, but has the second lowest official ranking. This leaves him carrying far less weight than the early market principals, and that could make a difference over this 2m 7f trip. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

Dalileo, a 10-year-old, can be relied upon around here with 10 out of 15 first three finishes. He won this race last year following a return from a similar break he has today. 4lb higher this time but still has serious claims, and any rain won't dampen his chance.

Ideally suited by trip when landing a handicap by 2L off 96 over 3m3f here last time. Idled in front a touch that day. Goes well here. Down in trip, probably a bit to come. Bowen takes the ride with a nice record.

Maillot Blanc has been running fair races without quite threatening to win, including a couple of decent efforts here lately. He’s on a workable mark and capable of running into a place if things fall right, and is my solid each-way shot

Malangen should have come on some for his first run in 5 months last time and steps up to three miles today. At the age of 10, he may find this trip now suits him better, having finished in the frame over three miles previously. He has a solid course record, and the overall consistent profile he has gives him strong place claims at least.

He's just 2 lbs above what he defied to win this race last season. Coming into this off the back of a solid run last time out. He won this race by a narrow margin last term, repelling the leader Hang In There right on the line, beating him by a neck. A proper ding-dong battle up the home straight. To be fair, the winner threw it away, carrying his head awkwardly after making a mistake at the last flight. He then went on to finish a solid 3rd in the Summer Plate at Market Rasen next time out off a 9 lbs higher mark (7 lbs higher than his current mark), beaten just 5 lengths by the winner Sure Touch. That form has been franked since with the 2nd subsequently winning a Grade 2. His most recent run over course and distance was solid, bumping into a well-handicapped mare called Coco Mademoiselle, beaten just over 2 lengths. The winner is on a steep upward curve, so no disgrace there at all. If he runs a similar race here, he is bang there.

Sits 5lbs above the mark he ran a cracker off lto. Going into calmer waters here. With James Bowen booked to ride. 
He ran a solid race in a competitive handicap at the Punchestown festival. Finishing a running on 2nd behind easy winner James Du Berlais.. He had no chance with the winner already away and gone. But I liked the way he stayed on. It offered plenty of encouragement going forward. 
His run at Leopardstown in 2024 rates the standout single piece of form in this field. He finished a clear 2nd behind easy winner Heart Wood in an ultra competitive handicap. Beaten 14L by the winner. That horse has subsequently finished 2nd in a pair of Grade 1 races. With the most recent 2nd coming in the Ryanair at the Cheltenham festival back in March. He bumped into Fact To File. 
He's got a nice racing weight here. Comes into this off the back of a solid run lto. He should be there abouts in this type of race.

Wide open race this and I can 4 out that I like but one that has caught my eye and the odds might be too big is Ballintubber Boy. Before the Ludlow runs he was a good winner at Huntington setting a good time as well whilst doing so. Also if you delve a little deeper into those Ludlow runs they don't actually read that bad as first glance. I think he is priced too big and worth a shot. 10/1

High class performer who is at the veteran stage of his career but still produced a quality performance to land the Summer Cup at Uttoxeter last year. Highly tried during the winter (4th in the Charlie Hall) but this is more his bag so should run very well this afternoon.

ANNSAM has won four hurdle races and four chases from 1m 7f to 3m. Third in a chase over 3m at Perth on his latest outing in April. Course, distance, and going should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.
The trainer has got two entered in this race as they are stepping this one back up in trip with the same 5 lbs claimer on board, as this is his only ride of the day. A good value each-way bet.

Patrick Neville's horses are running well. The Last Cloud won a maiden hurdle here last time in a faster time than Just Dottie, who won a handicap hurdle on the same card carrying slightly less weight. So he can beat the mare and follow up with his second win.

Heart Above won twice last season, including once over C&D, and 3 of his last four starts have been among the places. At a career-high weight, going up another 3lb, but is open to improvement. At 6/1 with extra places available at some bookmakers, it's a great each-way shout.

Sean Bowen retains the winning ride on Just Dottie in a bid for a hat-trick today. Although the penalty makes it more difficult, it will be offset by a drop in class today. With the champion jockey abroad again, it should enable another success.

Good run in a better class race Lto over today's C/D, yet drops another 4lb today so is very nicely treated back in this class 4 grade off that mark. Good conditional back up claiming 7lb and very good trainer is tops here numerically last 5 seasons, making current 8/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Trailblazer is holding his form well and ran respectably again at Sedgefield last time out. The return to a visor could sharpen him up in this sort of company. But he is not the easiest to win with consistently, so he is my lively each-way player in this field.

BRINGSTY has improved on the Flat since his four qualifying runs over hurdles and the books look to have taken a big risk pricing him so big on his handicap hurdle debut. Trainer landed quite the gamble in the 4:05 at Hexham (Saturday), so the market will be telling.

GARRICK PAINTER has a decent flat rating potentially making him a well treated handicap hurdler. This Irish yard landed a huge gamble in this sphere with a similarly low grade racer with modest form yesterday and this one could be interesting if the money started to come.

Unexposed 6yo, three hurdle runs. Runner-up in a maiden hurdle over this C/D four weeks ago, no answer at the finish behind a 108 rated winner - the third has run well since. Room for improvement, an opening handicap mark of 95 should give him every chance in this weak looking contest.

The model I run suggests Jet Patrol can win this one. Jet Patrol lines up here with the highest RPR of this larger 14 horse race. Jet Patrol has an official ranking that leaves him well treated off this mark and therefore goes out carrying 11 lbs less than the other market leaders. Jet Patrol comes here in decent form, having come 2nd on the 13th of May and having run out 4th only 14 days ago. Race fitness should not be a concern. The model has indicated a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

Found myself attracted to AWAY SHE GOES now that it’s doubled in price. Going right-handed has to help. Unlucky with all the dolled-off hurdles last time out, and it’s just always nice to have a front runner on your side.
Shadowfax of Rohan ran well on handicap debut over this course and distance, coming in third. Didn't like the longer distance last time, so worth a chance back down in trip.
Flat winner who has placed in 2 of 4 hurdle starts. Runs off the same mark as when finishing 3rd last time, and a similar performance gives an each-way chance again.

Generally regressive since leaving Keith Dalgleish almost two years ago, but did show a little more on his second run for a mark over hurdles. Very well treated on the pick of his flat form, so he has to be worth giving another chance to now that he starts handicapping over hurdles from a lowly mark.

Local trainer Jean McGregor almost trained an 80-1 shock winner at Perth last month, where Ivynator, running from out of the handicap in a two and a half mile conditional jockeys' handicap hurdle, travelled strongly throughout but eventually finished 2nd. That was the seven-year-old horse's first decent form, and it has pushed him back into the handicap here on a mark of 74. Peter Kavanagh retains the ride, dropping in distance to two miles.

A Fair Maiden competing on the flat for Mark Prescott had limited impact in his three novice/maiden hurdle starts over the last month, always starting at long odds. He appears to be aimed at handicaps and is a great candidate for an each-way bet at 33/1, particularly with both the trainer and jockey in excellent shape.

Was beaten just over a length when finishing second when stepped up to today's trip at Uttoxeter last month when returning from almost three months off. Has a good record over fences with three wins and seven places from his thirteen starts (77% win/place strike rate). Should be thereabouts.

Hardy Diamond seems on a decent mark for this chase handicap debut and is worth a chance that she can handle the new trip. She does get Sean Bowen to help out and could go well if getting to the post.

Five wins and a runner-up spot from the last seven outings, including two wins over the larger obstacles around today's trip. Takes a drop in class here today following a good second at Market Rasen last time out. Looks to have strong claims here running off the same mark.
Won a hunter chase over course and distance last month by 12 lengths. This will be a little harder but remains on the same mark and could go well.

Wasdell Dundalk is a better chaser than hurdler. His latest start after 133 days off over hurdles was very likely a sharpener before going back over fences today. Drops to class 4 in this sphere for the first time in a year. The four-time course winner, who acts on any ground, can prove a different proposition today. McMenamin is 5/15 on the 10-year-old.
Ganapathi ran three close 2nds prior to a lackluster sixth over course and distance six weeks ago. I find it interesting that Craig Nichol takes his first ride on the 9-y-o.

Hamish may be getting long in the tooth as a nine-year-old, but he gets his favoured going at Goodwood and starts off the season in a Listed race. Although the opposition looks strong, he is top-rated and should stay on to win on rain-softened going.
Ended last season with a Listed win on AW. Beaten 7 1/4 in The King's Cup (Group 3) at Bahrain last time in March. Generally in good form. Trainer's in form. Value selection based on balance of form.

The only one who has had a race in the last month is Bolster, who made his reappearance in a Group 2 on unsuitably fast ground at Chester. He took the graduation from handicaps up to Listed company with some aplomb in November. The four-year-old was a solid 7/4 favourite at Newmarket over ten furlongs on soft ground and battled on well to prevail. That form is holding up quite well, and Sons And Lovers was mixing it with Jan Breughel next time at the Curragh. If Hamish was 100% race-fit, he would be odds-on.

Lightly raced 4-year-old colt, ex-German trained. He won the German Derby on his penultimate start last year. He followed that with a respectable 6th in a Group 1 race won by the smart 123-rated 'Rebel's Romance'. Now trained at the John Gosden yard, and he can be a player at this Listed level.

I am really not sure why this ex-Fabre horse is 20-1, but I'll take the chance. Will love the going today, and at least one of these I am not sure will. Bolster trying the trip for the first time. Hamish is now a 9-year-old, and I'm not sure either of Gosden's horses would want heavy going. Trained now by Nicky Henderson, so I suppose he could just be using this as a fitness run. But in a 5-runner race, I will go with an each-way at this price.

I'm not sure about the odds of 2-1. That's short for a handicap. Nariko has a lot of ability and trainer Hugo Palmer will probably have been waiting for soft ground to run this 4yo filly by Night Of Thunder. Smart winner on soft at Haydock 6f just over a year ago beating Kodi Lion 2 lengths there (it was a strong handicap). Followed that with a win at Salisbury and neck second at Doncaster. Strange the stable hasn't tried this filly in higher grade company as she obviously has ability. Still well handicapped off OR84 (not even top weight) and has a big shout.

It's worth taking on the current odds-on favorite here who hasn't won over this distance and has yet to run on this course. Racingbreaks Ryder has run here five times and placed on three occasions and was 2nd on heavy ground over a mile. It's forecast heavy ground again today and drops back to his favorite trip of 7 furlongs and is currently 6 lb below his highest winning mark. Trainer and jockey are in form, so it looks a good e/w bet at 4/1 to a slight loss if placed if all eight go to post. Win only if another non-runner.

Won on final race last year on soft going and hasn't really fired in two runs this year. Hoping the current fav will be needing this first run of the season and Dapper Valley will improve on this going today.

Only had 2 runs on Aw since joining this stable from M. Hammond, but was a winner/run well on very soft ground for that yard. Has dropped to a very attractive mark of 72 for this level, good jockey booked and shrewd trainer best here with his 4yo plus @ 15 percent last 5 seasons, making current 9/1 very good Ew value against the hot favourite in the race.

Three time winner on the all weather and has been running well this winter and looks well handicapped returning to turf. Has only run twice on the turf but given French sire maybe the decent ground was against him and heavy going here might work the oracle. Was touched off in a handicap on the AW off a mark of 77 so might be worth chancing off 76 here with different conditions today. Yard had a 25-1 winner pop up recently and owner has had success with the Dow yard. Wasn't beaten far recently over C&D and was only 1/2 length behind Mister Bluebird there who I fancy can go well earlier on the card. If he does this one might well shorten so get on early I say.

Low drawn runners should hold a decent advantage here on soft ground, and this outsider drawn 2 could well be the answer. He looked impressive when winning a maiden in Ireland on soft, hitting the line hard to beat a horse that won its next race easily. The horse has had 2 runs on the AW for a new trainer, but a return to soft ground looks like exactly what is required to return to winning ways.
If he can bounce back from his less impactful run at Haydock, his profile suggests a genuine threat, especially with James Doyle booked.

Knebworth was third here last month on good ground and could be worth a shot, as all his wins have been with a bit more give in the ground. He is now just 1 lb above his last winning mark on soft ground.
3rd over the distance here at Goodwood 16 days ago. Stepping back to 6f should suit better. Drops 1lb in the mark. Versatile on any ground. Solid each way chance.
This one is returning from a break as they are dropping it down in class/grade with the regular jockey back on board. A good value each way bet.

Small each-way tip for this selection, definitely needs improvement but with the ground conditions being very testing at Goodwood today, it could throw up some strange results. Gunfighter hasn't had much racing since returning from a rest so may well have a bit more to offer yet. If coping with the testing ground, could be running well.

Tattycoram has form figures of 3-314, and although not running her best race in a Group 3 at York, this is a lower level and could well have a chance. With Rossa Ryan booked as jockey, she has a great chance to be in the places.
A non-runner on the 24th of May when fancied to win but withdrawn for unsuitable ground. Soft ground is forecast today at Goodwood and is a big positive. It should run a big race.

07/06/2025 Last Updated. Place a bet at 1/4pt your normal stake. Probability of winning is 42%. Running style held up at 67%. Actual win% is 33%. Actual place% is 50%. My win odds are 4/1. My place odds are 7/1.

Won on very soft ground as a 2yo and followed that up with a decent run under similar conditions in a listed race @ Newmarket. Decent run on Aw @ Southwell on 3yo comeback, nice pedigree states that step up to this 1.2 miles a plus, very under used jockey up (J. Crowley rides for this retainer here) and very good trainer is 33 percent with his runners here last 5 seasons, making current 7/1 very good Ew value in the race.

Kingman filly El Budoor is going the right way. A late starter who debuted at Ascot last month and was not asked much. Stepped up markedly on that when, having been fractious and thrown her jockey pre-race, produced a solid win beating a decent sort at Lingfield on second maiden start. Considerably up in class now but seems progressive. Pedigree offers hope. Her dam Enbihaar won three of three races at Goodwood all at Class 1 level in these owners' silks. Gosden stable in very good form (SR 26%). Jim Crowley rides. Some market support.

Decent winner last time on the all-weather, and although she may not be up to winning this, a place isn't out of the realms of possibility. Her two career wins have come at 20-1 and 9-1, and she has also previously finished a neck second at 10-1, so I wouldn't be put off by the big odds either.

The Gosden-trained Queen Of Thieves is a big price at 16's at the time of writing. Granted, she has a couple of pounds to find with a couple of these runners. The 3-year-old Frankel filly is open to improvement, and providing she handles the ground, then I think she could outrun her odds.

Anna Swan showed plenty when winning at Newbury as a two-year-old on soft ground over 7 furlongs. She was pitched into the Fillies' Mile Group 1, which was over-ambitious in October. Then her comeback run last month was underwhelming in the Pretty Polly, but she was probably lacking race fitness on ground which was too quick. With her preferred conditions today, a better run today should be forthcoming.

A fairly weak listed event, but I thought Quebella’s run behind Brise Noir had a bit more substance to it than meets the eye. That horse went on to run a decent race in France, just behind Poschiavo, who has some fair form in the book in and around 100-rated animals. That puts this horse in the right sort of ballpark for a race like this and certainly has her overpriced. Strong at the line last time and staying strong on her debut, she should appreciate a strong pace, which looks likely, and her action suggests to me a horse that will appreciate some dig in the ground.

Aggagio loves Goodwood and soft going. He had three wins and a short-head second in 2022 here on soft going. This season, he has run respectably here on good, ridden by seven-pound claiming Ashley Lewis, and should perform much better here on soft.
Distance winner. 3rd in the race last year and is now 2lb below that mark, so runs off 89. Only 1lb higher than his last winning mark. Top jockey Oisin Murphy on board, solid bid to win the race.

Almuhit has been a different horse over hurdles since wind surgery, notching up two wins in his last two races for Gary Brown, and then running a cracking second of twenty-five at Punchestown in April. Reportedly took a false step over C&D sixteen days ago on yard debut, so connections must be confident in bringing him back today.
Trainer Faye Bramley has got off to a wonderful start in her career with four winners and five places from only eleven runs and I think it's about time jockey Edward Greatrix had another winner as it's 25 rides since his last winner.

ZINC WHITE runs for a yard who do well with staying handicappers on the level and who have been among the recent winners. The booking today of jockey Jim Crowley could be a sign of intent and proven most effective when returning from a huge absence he can figure.

Ex French trained who was a winner on heavy/very soft ground over there and did not run that badly in the Chester Cup Lto. The booking of R. Ryan here would suggest connections expecting a big run and worth noting that top NH trainer does not run that many on the flat, making current 7/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Has not been seen since finishing 3rd at Chester in May 2023. Has won over this course and distance, and if returning with the same ability, has at least an each-way chance.

Good Show hasn’t been seen in nearly two years and was well beaten on his last outing. So why have I tipped him? Well, a new yard change and two years to get a horse ready is not uncommon. Yes, we do not know what state the horse is in, but not ruled out entirely here as he is on his last winning mark. Small EW here.

With the absence of three of these, most notably Stella Sunrise, this looks a good opportunity for Poatan to get off the mark. Promising third on debut at Beverley over 5f. Will improve for that outing and should be good enough to win this one.

Jel Pepper comes from a yard that had their first juvenile winner of the season last week, and there has been support for this one also. A well-bred sort, he must be doing it correctly at home and can run a big race.
Song Of The Clyde could well be in the mix. He boasts a sharp 5f pedigree, full brother to a useful sprinter. An eye-catching £85,000 buy with potential to shine early at Sprint trips.
The six furlongs, drop in class, and the ease in the ground could well be what AHEAD OF FASHION needs.
A newcomer for the Simcock yard, Havana Grey's half-brother, related to 3 winners, and J P Spencer's only ride today. He probably doesn't have a full booking these days. E/W tickle.
Has been running in higher class races of late and is sure to appreciate this drop in standard. Can get off the mark at the fourth attempt.
Second last time out at Beverley was a significant improvement from 11th on debut at Doncaster and now makes a big step up in class hoping to continue that improvement.

Worth a shot at these odds. It's a very open race, this one. It was a very promising debut effort last time out when finishing 4th at Redcar over 6f. Travelled well for the majority and led but couldn't quite hold on. This shorter trip may suit and won't be far away.

Beaten favorite last time at Wolverhampton over 5f when sent off 100/30 fav but trailed home a disappointing 9th of 10. Probably went too hard early that day and faded badly. It didn't look good but can get back on track here in a wide-open contest.

Coul Jane didn't run too badly over 6f last time out, not sure if this drop down to 5f will suit or not but, the testing ground conditions at Goodwood today may bring this horse into it. Still has time for improvement.

Has had issues @ start on 2 runs to date, but has now been gelded which should sort their temprement problem. Did well on 2nd run as they were well behind before making some decent late headway, so today's heavy ground could hold up a few front runners and bring selection back them, making current 11/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Spanish Harlem has not won in fourteen races since joining Willie Mullins from France where he won his first race over hurdles. He has been running in valuable handicap races over marathon distances recently and this looks his easiest chance to win his first chase for some time.

The model I run suggests Baltic Bird can win this one. Baltic Bird lines up here with the second highest RPR and carries slightly more weight than the others for the trouble. Ran a good race 34 days ago to come first and so comes here in good form and race condition. Patrick O'Brien on board relieves 7 lbs for claiming, but so do other jockeys involved in the race. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which has largely been driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Promise to take from all of his starts over fences without getting a hard ride in any of them. It’s likely that handicaps like this one will see him in a much better light and looks to have been found a good opportunity to get off the mark over the larger obstacles.

Lisnagar Fortune ran his best chase performance yet last time over course and distance in a Listed handicap chase when finishing in 3rd place. This looks an easier task despite a two-pound rise in his mark.

Ho My Lord was slightly disappointing last time when only fourth at Kilbeggan, having been sent off as a well-fancied favorite. That said, the switch to handicaps could bring about improvement, especially if he settles better. Still unexposed over fences and has potential to figure here and win or each-way claims if jumping well today.
Has a nice little chance going by the recent Limerick win and 4th place last time in a hot handicap at Ballinrobe. Mc Kenna on board releases 5 lbs.

In Excelsis Deo had a fine 2022 and 2023 with Harry Fry but went off the boil last year, only beating one horse in his last four runs, which included a pulled-up and unseated rider. Owner J P McManus has probably said enough is enough and has moved the 7-y-o to Enda Bolger's yard. The stable is in good form of late with five winners and eight places from their last forty runners (four winners from the last ten). Jockey K E Buckley has been in fine form too with six winners and seven places from his last forty rides. I wish I knew the trainer's record with new additions, but if he can get In Excelsis Deo right, we could witness a resurgence. I'll never forget the horses 3rd of 11 at Cheltenham where he bounded up the hill, so I think he'll be well suited to Punchestown's gradual rise to the finish.Is TS and RPR top-rated on old form.
Must Be Obeyed could well be in the mix. She has solid course experience and placed form at this trip. Yet to win at the distance, but she's not ruled out.

Keep Up won a bumper before being stepped up to listed class last time out, where it finished a creditable 3rd. It is sure to have been well-schooled for this hurdle debut, and the market is speaking strongly for it.

Mi Lucky Cailin has been struggling to recapture her form and hasn't hit the frame in a long time. She made little impact last time, and a mistake didn’t help matters 3 out. The longer trip could bring something out of her, and with the jockey claimer of 5 pounds and another 1 pound lighter here (6 off in total), she may bounce back.

She is a point winner who ran a fine 3rd/9 over a similar trip on her reappearance at Killarney when beaten by 3 lengths. She was beaten by 8 lengths when 2nd/15 at Limerick over a shorter trip last month. However, back up in trip is likely to suit, and she is open to further progress.

The model I run suggests an upset from Kilrush Lady. This result has been driven by Kilrush Lady having a comparatively high RPR compared to the rest of the 19-runner field and is not punished for it in the weights as all horses line up with the exact same weight to carry. Wear cheekpieces for the first time to aid concentration and actually won last time out, albeit that form is hard to rely on with such a large break to the prior run. Has not run in 328 days and needs to go well fresh to get the job done. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator, which is driven by the small gap back to second but offset with a 'good value' price. This translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Not a bad effort from this horse when finishing 5th of 16 in a Maiden race last time out which was over a shorter distance than today's race, outpaced at times last time so this step up in distance may be more suitable. Still very early days for this horse so it's difficult to rule out some improvement at some point. Very small each-way tip.

Still a maiden after 10 starts, though has shown improved form in the last 2 runs. Particularly when only beaten 1.25 lengths when second over a furlong further at Wexford last month, with the front two in the race pulling well clear of the field. Should have every chance on that form.

Warm In Gorey is a 7-year-old gelding trained by P J Rothwell. He is a three-time winner over hurdles and sits some 4lb above his last winning mark on a 100. He has shown a liking for Punchestown, finishing 14-1-2 in three starts, and is a CD winner. He could contend off just 10st 1lb with Miss L Costello taking off a valuable 7lb.

Harry's Dream can go well for the Philip Rothwell yard. Harry's Dream has run a place in a couple of races and has had time off since a run at Limerick in March. It can do better off a good handicap rating today.

Going for a wildcard here with 4 places on offer. Divilabother was a bit disappointing at Sligo last time but had been shaping with more promise prior to that and could easily bounce back here. Stays this trip fine and handles today's ground. He might run better than his last run suggests and he has a jockey claimer of 7 off today. May grab a place here.

Paddy (Philip) Rothwell stable has come back into form with recent winners after a slight lull. The yard runs two here with similar profiles, both having returned with first run for some months at Tipperary last month. Warm In Gorey won this race in 2023. Oh, ok, there's a third stable runner in the picture! Woodstream Lad is the selection. Pippa (?) Elvin is the most experienced of the jockeys booked. The 8yo by Soldier Of Fortune ran a big race when second at Leopardstown in November 2023. Two wins either side of that. Runs off 6lbs higher than last winning mark. Good race. Hands On and Rose Boum are others of note.

Lukers Tipple had a decent season over hurdles without winning, including two 2nd places in four runs. He ran in the Fred Winter at the Cheltenham Festival and on the flat in April, beaten a neck in 2nd place. Should get his first win.

The model I run suggests Mick Collins can win this one. Mick Collins lines up here with the highest RPR of this 14-horse field and does not look to be penalized for it in the weights. All horses, bar a few, line up with the exact same initial amount of weight to carry over this 2m maiden hurdle. This is a very inexperienced lineup, but Mick Collins has some of the most experience on offer here and will come on well for the last run out 29 days ago, where a reasonable 5th might prove valuable. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.
Finished 3rd on her hurdles debut over 17f at Tipperary three weeks ago despite a rather mixed round of jumping. There should be more to come on that evidence and looks to have decent claims.

Unexposed having only raced twice under Rules. On the face of it, they look like poor runs but he went off 2/1 fav for his bumper debut run (2m 2f) and was leading up to 1 furlong out before fading quickly. He went off 8/1 for his hurdle debut (2m 4f) and was running well before a bad mistake sending him sprawling 3 furlongs out. Judging by the SP's on those runs, better is expected and he's worth another chance at big odds in this fairly weak race.

TATATEO is a 77 rated flat horse from his time spent on the level in Britain , so he should have enough ability to show up well in a maiden hurdle of this nature having now moved to an Irish yard. He did have a look around Killarney in a race won by the trainer's other runner which is interesting , so apparently with the yard looking for theIr runners to break their maidens early under this code he could surprise.

Il Pirata showed me a bit to work with when sixth on debut in a Ballinrobe bumper just under two weeks ago, staying on steadily in the closing stages. That experience won’t be lost on him and now he switches to hurdles. Each-way chance at very good odds here. Small stakes at 50/1, obviously.

The twice-raced Joli Travail won on its debut in France before joining the top Willie Mullins yard. It must have had a few problems to start but ran well enough after an absence to run 3rd in a maiden hurdle last time out. That run is sure to have brought the horse on, and it should go well.

The model I run suggests William Butler can win this one. William Butler lines up with the highest RPR of this large 17-horse race and carries the exact same weight as every other runner. All jockeys on board have varying claiming amounts, but Jake Coen on board relieves 3 lbs for William Butler. Good run out 25 days ago and placed in third. Looks to go one better here today. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which is largely driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Jazz De Cotte ran very well at Downpatrick, looking to be a good prospect in the making when second to Hills of Glory on 23 May. This race doesn't look as competitive as the Downpatrick race, in my opinion. Gordon Elliot has long-term ambitions for this horse, and he wants a win from him. So on Sunday, Jazz De Cotte is fancied by the yard to shed that maiden tag.

Winner of a Point to Point Maiden at Dromahane on debut. That came on yielding ground over a trip of three miles. Now making hurdles debut. Trained by Johnathan Sweeney with Paul O'Connor on board. Should improve from an impressive Points win.

Mister Frostie ran his best race so far when fourth at Downpatrick last time. He may have found the finish coming too soon and may be suited by this step up in distance. He's the choice to improve again and remain competitive.

Colm Murphy's 6-year-old has been crying out for this sort of trip and should not be missed now. He really caught the eye coming from nowhere to finish third here at the Festival over half a mile shorter.

Trained by Ollie McKiernan and has G.Noonan claiming 5 lbs on board. Has been running consistently well prior to a two month break. One win and three places in last six runs. Looks to have a decent each way chance in a wide open event.

Claimer of 3 and raised 2 by handicapper equals minus 1 pound lower here. Howdoyalikeherhome shaped with promise when third in a big-field handicap at Listowel last week, traveling well in first-time blinkers. That run looked good to me, and with her yard in fine form, she’s a strong each-way player who wouldn’t be a surprise winner either.

Ross O'Sullivan is another trainer coming back into form. A chance is taken on Club Manager here. Won and placed in low grade staying handicaps for Andrew Balding, a win and numerous decent efforts over hurdles for Gavin Cromwell before joining current trainer. Only five years old. Just one hurdle outing for the yard over 2m1f at Wexford last month. This is a big step up in trip but, by Nathaniel, Club Manager might come good for it. Handicap mark of 111 (11 stone 3 lbs) looks a bit tough so Tom Harney's 5lbs claim useful. An intriguing one.

This horse is a previous course winner over 2m 4f back in January this year, she has no problems with this longer distance of 3 miles , still fairly unexposed at this distance so it's difficult to rule out some improvement over this trip. Ran well in defeat after sitting too far back in the pack in the early stages of her last race but, still showed enough to think she's capable of running well today , each-way tip for today's NAP selection. Extra places available each-way in this race. Current rating looks fair, can be competitive from this rating , trip and ground conditions ideal and she's already proven at this course.

Thomas Mullins’ 6-year-old gelding CORAL RIVER makes his handicap bow here after a respectable run 39 days ago at the Punchestown Festival in what was undeniably deep company. At one stage, this son of OL' MAN RIVER looked completely outpaced and in trouble, but he dug deep, showed a ton of grit, and rallied strongly finishing third - staying on gamely when others faltered. That run was full of promise, and now he takes a notable drop in class.
He does carry top weight, but that burden is significantly eased by the 7lb claim of jockey Anna McGuinness, who is riding well with a 44% place strike rate over the past fortnight. That could be a crucial advantage, particularly in a field where very few look progressive. This is also trainer Thomas Mullins’ only runner on the card, which may indicate some degree of confidence.
The trip today is a bit of an unknown, but based on his staying effort last time out, it shouldn't be a negative. At odds of 18/1, there's definite each-way appeal. With the form in the book and a strong jockey claim, this looks worth a nibble in what could be a much easier task.

Could go well at a price here. Drops a couple of pounds and can be excused her last run, having been shuffled back and rider easy on her. Her penultimate start, she very much caught the eye when going well, only to meet interference at a crucial stage of the race. Worth an each-way bet here.

Westerner mare who ran a solid 4th/20 on her course debut at this venue back in January before picking up her first career win when romping home by over 4 lengths at Fairyhouse back in February. She has been freshened up, and despite a 6lb rise, she is receiving weight all round today. Each/way chance.

NAVIGATOR JACK has potential to stay this more extreme distance in the handicap hurdles sphere and he has the benefit of a reappearance run behind him now. He has a pedigree which points towards this test potentially unlocking some improvement , so he can be considered from some intriguing outsiders.

Brosna Queen is a full sister to the very useful Queens Gamble, and she showed a lot of promise at the Punchestown Festival 6 weeks ago, finishing a never nearer 5th in what is usually a very good bumper. Queens Gamble prefers good ground, so the ground should be fine, and she has the assistance this time of Patrick Mullins in the saddle.

The model I run suggests Kabylia can win this one. Lines up here with the highest RPR of the 13-runner field and is not penalized for it in the weights. We have a split initial amount of weight being carried with half the field carrying 11-11 and the other half 11-4. I don't think this is enough difference to make up for the lack of experience where it appears to be the lower weight is for horses who haven't run before. Experience matters more than the weight difference in this scenario, and Kabylia can build on the good recent form figures of 751-2, where that second only came 26 days ago. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Amboyna is lightly raced but reliable, placing in sole attempt at this trip. Proven on similar ground, she has potential under a capable amateur in a competitive field.

Flemensfirth mare who was well beaten on her bumper debut last September, but the selection showed a huge improvement when returning off a 262-day break, romping home by three lengths in a bumper at Limerick last month. The stable is in good form, and jockey A P Ryan retains the ride. He is currently 3-8, each/way chance.

Ran well on 2nd start over hurdles Lto @ Thurles in a maiden hurdle, so interesting why connections are reverting to this sphere of racing, where trainer is 1/2 last 5 seasons, making current 50/1 worth Ew consideration in the race.

QUIZZINI represents a shrewd Irish operation and this mare makes her career debut with a family boasting bundles of stamina. That clearly reads well and the yard often punt their runners if they have one ready. The post-time market can help us.
